- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16) and prices are falling, model often overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; allow slight lagged rebound.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak to avoid overreaction.  
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% if recent 18-day average is > 65.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.27, -0.16, +0.23), model misreads trend — smooth forecast with weighted average of recent 5–7 days.  
- In 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period reversals — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment turns positive after 20–25 days.
